messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am working on a large simulation and ran into memory troubles. I saw that the reference for creating monitors explained "For large simulations, or if the RAM footprint is an issue, you may consider monitoring to disk".

Using monitor_csv() did solve my memory issue, but after a while, I got a new error saying "Warning in file.create(unlist(files)) : unable to create '...\Local\Temp\Rtmp0ujqEX\file69b026aa3dd0_arrivals.csv' (and releases, attributes, resources) because of too many open files".

So I guess I need to close/delete the files created with monitor_csv(). I saw in the reference that the "finalize" argument is "an optional function to be called when the object is destroyed. For example, monitor_mem does not require any finalizer, but monitor_delim and monitor_csv use this to remove the created files when the monitor is destroyed", but I have no idea how to use this.

I also saw that the "keep" argument is "whether to keep files on exit. By default, files are removed", I am guessing this refers to exiting the whole R session?

Thanks for any help!

On Mon, 4 Apr 2022 at 14:44, SQ3 W23 <shuqi...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hello,
>
> I am working on a large simulation and ran into memory troubles. I saw that the reference for creating monitors explained "For large simulations, or if the RAM footprint is an issue, you may consider monitoring to disk".

> Using monitor_csv() did solve my memory issue, but after a while, I got a new error saying "Warning in file.create(unlist(files)) : unable to create '...\Local\Temp\Rtmp0ujqEX\file69b026aa3dd0_arrivals.csv' (and releases, attributes, resources) because of too many open files".

Are you running many many simulations in parallel? Or are you keeping
a lot of simulation environments around? It would be nice to have a
small reproducible example of this issue. I don't know what's the
limit on Windows, but I would say that it should be hard to hit.

> So I guess I need to close/delete the files created with monitor_csv(). I saw in the reference that the "finalize" argument is "an optional function to be called when the object is destroyed. For example, monitor_mem does not require any finalizer, but monitor_delim and monitor_csv use this to remove the created files when the monitor is destroyed", but I have no idea how to use this.

Don't worry about the finalize argument. monitor_csv handles that for
you (it's just a call to unlink). You should avoid accumulating a
large number of simulation environments around. But maybe there's some
environment leak in some place and objects are not properly destroyed.
We have seen this in the past with magrittr, so you could try the same
with the new pipe in base R.

> I also saw that the "keep" argument is "whether to keep files on exit. By default, files are removed", I am guessing this refers to exiting the whole R session?

In general, it means when the object is destroyed. This happens when
the R session ends, but if you rm() the simulation environment (or
another thing is assigned to the same variable name), files should be
removed automatically too.

Iñaki

messages.body_plain:
Hi Iñaki,

Thanks for the suggestions! I am running a large number of simulations, but not in parallel, just using lapply. I have a number of scenarios, and in each scenario the simulation is run for a number of replications. In addition, this is meant to be part of a shiny app, so the whole thing could be run multiple times.

Here is an example based on one of the vignettes:

library(simmer) #I'm using version 4.4.4

mk.env<-function(time) { #a single simulation
  mon <- monitor_csv()
  hospital <- simmer("Hospital Process",mon=mon)

  patient <- trajectory("patients' path") %>%
    set_attribute("rand", function() {rnorm(1)}) %>%
  ## add an intake activity
  seize("nurse", 1) %>%
  timeout(function() rnorm(1, 15)) %>%
  release("nurse", 1) %>%
  ## add a consultation activity
  seize("doctor", 1) %>%
  timeout(function() rnorm(1, 20)) %>%
  release("doctor", 1) %>%
  ## add a planning activity
  seize("administration", 1) %>%
  timeout(function() rnorm(1, 5)) %>%
  release("administration", 1)

  hospital %>%
    add_resource("nurse", 1) %>%
    add_resource("doctor", 2) %>%
    add_resource("administration", 1) %>%
    add_generator("patient", patient, function() rnorm(1, 10, 2)) %>%
    run(time)
}

mk.reps<-function(days,times) { #run the simulation for a number of replications in one scenario
  env<-lapply(1:times,function(i) {
    mk.env(days)
  })
  dat<-get_mon_arrivals(env,per_resource=TRUE)
  rm(env)  #in my actual simulation, this also helped with memory usage, but I'm not sure if it applies to this simulation
  gc()
  return(dat)
}

mk.scen<-function(days,times,n_scenarios) { #run a number of scenarios
  dat<-lapply(1:n_scenarios,function(i) {
    mk.reps(days,times)
  })
  return(dat)
}

days<-100
times<-10
n_scenarios<-4

lapply(1:2,function(i) { #for example, user might choose two different sets of scenarios to run
  mk.scen(days,times,n_scenarios)
})

This runs without any problem for the first time. However, it runs into the "too many open files" problem on the second time.

I saw in this question Is there a limit on number of open files in Windows <https://stackoverflow.com/questions/870173/is-there-a-limit-on-number-of-open-files-in-windows> that "The C run-time libraries have a 512 limit for the number of files that can be open at any one time". I'm not sure if this is the limit that applies here though. From the warnings, it seems each replication makes 4 files (arrivals, releases, attributes, resources), so the total number of files created for running the above two times would be 4 files * 10 replications * 4 scenarios * 2 sets of scenarios * 2 times=640 files, which is just over the 512 limit. I also tried replacing "%>%" with "|>", but the problem persists. I will look into simmer.mon.

It seems this particular problem with opening too many files is just with Windows, since when the app is deployed to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, which uses Linux, I'm able to run this a lot more times without any problem.

But I have also been wondering in objects are not being destroyed. In my actual simulation, memory usage is accumulated each time this is run, but since I have put everything in functions, and also used rm(env) in the function for replications, I couldn't figure out why.

Thanks!

messages.body_plain:
Ok, I found the issue: you were rm'ing the environment, yes, but in a secondary function, not in the frame that creates the simulation environment in the first place. So in the mk.env function you have two issues: variables mon and hospital are kept in that frame, and thus the objects are not destroyed. This works for me:

library(simmer)

mk.env<-function(time) {
  hospital <- simmer("Hospital Process", mon=monitor_csv()) # do not assign the monitor to another variable, or rm it

  patient <- trajectory("patients' path") %>%
    set_attribute("rand", function() {rnorm(1)}) %>%
    ## add an intake activity
    seize("nurse", 1) %>%
    timeout(function() rnorm(1, 15)) %>%
    release("nurse", 1) %>%
    ## add a consultation activity
    seize("doctor", 1) %>%
    timeout(function() rnorm(1, 20)) %>%
    release("doctor", 1) %>%
    ## add a planning activity
    seize("administration", 1) %>%
    timeout(function() rnorm(1, 5)) %>%
    release("administration", 1)

  hospital %>%
    add_resource("nurse", 1) %>%
    add_resource("doctor", 2) %>%
    add_resource("administration", 1) %>%
    add_generator("patient", patient, function() rnorm(1, 10, 2)) %>%
    run(time)

  env <- wrap(hospital) # extract all the info
  rm(hospital) # rm the environment
  env # return the info

}

mk.reps<-function(days,times) { #run the simulation for a number of replications in one scenario
  env<-lapply(1:times,function(i) {
    mk.env(days)
  })
  dat<-get_mon_arrivals(env,per_resource=TRUE)

  return(dat)
}

mk.scen<-function(days,times,n_scenarios) { #run a number of scenarios
  dat<-lapply(1:n_scenarios,function(i) {
    mk.reps(days,times)
  })
  return(dat)
}

days<-100
times<-10
n_scenarios<-4

x <- lapply(1:10,function(i) { #for example, user might choose two different sets of scenarios to run
  mk.scen(days,times,n_scenarios)
})

So I'm closing https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/278.

Iñaki
